A1.justification: Both PDFs report the same AugCLIP study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original human-preference studies, ground-truth selection experiments, and ablations across five benchmarks, with further empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds editing-model rankings, an attribute-importance human study, and quantitative description-similarity results.

M1.justification: Equations 3–10 and Appendix B retain the same GPT-4V attribute extraction, relative weighting, weighted linear SVM, minimum-modification projection, and cosine scoring. The new weighting experiment evaluates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The five editing datasets and editing scenarios are retained. V3 adds an attribute-importance judgment task using DreamBooth examples (Section 6, Table 7), asking humans to compare attributes rather than edited-image quality.

E2.justification: V3 Table 7 introduces a naïve weighting comparator based on cosine similarity between an attribute and the text direction ΔT. The existing editing-metric comparators, including the Appendix D.3 GPT-4V comparison, remain.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a 10-participant, 40-scenario attribute-importance survey with paired choices and Pearson-correlation evaluation, plus model-ranking assessment and ROUGE-L comparison of descriptions. Existing benchmark sizes, the 105-participant image-preference study, and the CLIP backbone remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether attribute weights match human importance judgments and whether metric rankings reproduce human editing-model rankings (Tables 7 and 4). Description-randomness analysis gains ROUGE-L evidence; existing ablations, classifier comparisons, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds and human-alignment variance of 0.0197, with the same seed examples in Appendix A.2. V3 does not report increased repetitions or new uncertainty intervals or significance tests; Pearson correlation and ROUGE-L are added evaluation measures.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged after matching tables. V3 adds model rankings matching human rankings across three datasets, source/target importance correlations of 0.794/0.883 versus 0.394/0.637 for naïve weighting, and description ROUGE-L of 0.7590.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, classifier objectives, projection derivation, and appendix formulations are retained. Renaming the randomness discussion to include 'Equivariance' introduces no formal property or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: context-aware evaluation balancing preservation and modification, with strong human alignment across five benchmarks. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the computational-overhead limitation by explaining that reported time includes CLIP loading also required by other CLIP-based metrics. Existing mechanism explanations and Appendix E.6 limitations concerning subjective human preferences remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 promises a future code release; v3 states that code is available and supplies repository and project-page links. V3 also identifies TEdBench for the seed test and discloses 3.61-second CLIP loading and 8.62-second maximum attribute extraction. Appendix algorithms and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V3 removes Section 2's 'Metrics Used in Text-to-Image Generation' paragraph and its six references, including TIFA, GenEval, T2I-CompBench, and LLMScore. This narrows adjacent-work coverage while retaining the central positioning against image-editing metrics.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain unchanged. Limited edits condense the dataset/model explanation, remove one background paragraph, expand and rename the randomness discussion, add acknowledgements, and update affiliation and citation formatting.

P2.justification: V3 substantially retypesets the main text and references from one column to two, relocating and resizing figures and tables throughout. It adds Tables 4 and 7 and restructures the editing-scenario table into two blocks. Appendix figures are enlarged while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: The new model-ranking and attribute-importance studies directly strengthen evidence for practical metric utility and the weighting rationale. Code-access and timing disclosures improve reproducibility information while existing results and failure analyses remain available. Removing the text-to-image-metric discussion slightly reduces context, but the targeted validation and documentation provide a limited net improvement.
